```{r setup, include = FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
library(fmrigds)
set.seed(42)
```

A one-sample group analysis asks whether the mean of the subjects' contrast
maps differs from zero. Under the null hypothesis each subject's map is
symmetric about zero, so flipping the sign of a whole map leaves its
distribution unchanged. Flipping whole maps, not single voxels, keeps each
subject's spatial correlation intact. That is what makes the permutation null
valid for statistics that depend on spatial extent, such as threshold-free
cluster enhancement (TFCE) and cluster mass.

`reduce(method = "perm:onesample")` runs this test. With
`options$spatial`, it also computes TFCE and cluster family-wise error (FWER)
p-values from the same sign flips as the voxelwise max-T correction.

## A small example

We simulate 14 subjects on a 16 x 16 x 10 grid. Each map is smooth noise,
and a block of voxels carries a positive effect.

```{r simulate}
dims <- c(16L, 16L, 10L)
n_subj <- 14L
mask_idx <- seq_len(prod(dims))

smooth <- function(a) {
  # Average each voxel with its six neighbours, twice.
  for (it in 1:2) {
    b <- a
    b[-1, , ] <- b[-1, , ] + a[-dims[1], , ]
    b[-dims[1], , ] <- b[-dims[1], , ] + a[-1, , ]
    b[, -1, ] <- b[, -1, ] + a[, -dims[2], ]
    b[, -dims[2], ] <- b[, -dims[2], ] + a[, -1, ]
    b[, , -1] <- b[, , -1] + a[, , -dims[3]]
    b[, , -dims[3]] <- b[, , -dims[3]] + a[, , -1]
    a <- b / 7
  }
  a / sd(a)
}

effect <- array(0, dims)
effect[5:9, 5:9, 4:6] <- 1.2
beta <- vapply(seq_len(n_subj), function(s) {
  (smooth(array(rnorm(prod(dims)), dims)) + effect)[mask_idx]
}, numeric(length(mask_idx)))

g <- new_gds(
  assays = list(beta = array(beta, c(length(mask_idx), n_subj, 1L)),
                var = array(1, c(length(mask_idx), n_subj, 1L))),
  space = space_voxel(dims, affine = diag(c(2, 2, 2, 1)), mask_idx = mask_idx,
                      storage = "packed"),
  subjects = paste0("sub-", seq_len(n_subj)),
  contrasts = "task"
)
```

The analysis is one `reduce()` call. `spatial = c("tfce", "cluster")` asks
for both statistics. Clusters are formed at a one-tailed voxel p of 0.01
(`cluster_p`) and tested by excess mass, the sum of `z - threshold` over the
cluster.

```{r run}
res <- g |>
  reduce(method = "perm:onesample",
         options = list(n_perm = 1000, seed = 1, alternative = "greater",
                        spatial = c("tfce", "cluster"), cluster_p = 0.01)) |>
  compute()

names(assays(res))
```

The corrected maps are ordinary assays:

```{r maps}
inside <- as.vector(effect[mask_idx] > 0)
data.frame(
  region = c("effect block", "elsewhere"),
  min_p_maxT = c(min(assay(res, "p_fwer")[inside]), min(assay(res, "p_fwer")[!inside])),
  min_p_TFCE = c(min(assay(res, "p_tfce_fwer")[inside]), min(assay(res, "p_tfce_fwer")[!inside])),
  min_p_cluster = c(min(assay(res, "p_cluster_fwer")[inside]),
                    min(assay(res, "p_cluster_fwer")[!inside]))
)
```

Max-T only reaches the strongest voxels of the block; TFCE and cluster mass
pool evidence over its extent and give smaller p-values. Both spatial methods
also mark some voxels just outside the block: noise voxels above the
cluster-forming threshold that touch the block join its cluster and share its
p-value, and TFCE support spreads to such neighbours. A significant cluster
says that the cluster contains signal, not that every voxel in it does.

The null distributions and the cluster table are stored in an attachment.
Peaks are given as grid indices and as world coordinates from the space's
affine.

```{r clusters}
att <- metadata(res)$attachments[["reduce/perm:onesample/contrast=task"]]
head(att$clusters[, c("cluster_id", "size", "mass", "p_fwer_mass", "p_fwer_extent",
                      "peak_stat", "peak_x", "peak_y", "peak_z")])
quantile(att$null$tfce, 0.95)   # the 5% FWER TFCE threshold
```

`write_nifti_assays()` writes the maps for viewing, for example the TFCE
p-values and the cluster labels:

```{r export, eval = requireNamespace("RNifti", quietly = TRUE)}
out_dir <- tempfile("perm_maps")
manifest <- write_nifti_assays(res, out_dir,
                               assays = c("tfce", "p_tfce_fwer", "cluster_id"))
basename(manifest$path)
```

## Options

| option | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `spatial` | none | `"tfce"`, `"cluster"` or both |
| `alternative` | `"two.sided"` | tail for every corrected map; two-sided uses both tails |
| `n_perm`, `seed` | 5000, none | number of sign flips; seed for reproducibility |
| `spatial_stat` | `"z"` | z-equivalent of t (`"z"`) or t itself (`"t"`, as in FSL randomise) |
| `tfce_H`, `tfce_E`, `tfce_dh` | 2, 0.5, 0.1 | TFCE height and extent exponents, height step |
| `cluster_p` / `cluster_threshold` | 0.001 | cluster-forming threshold as a one-tailed p, or on the statistic's scale |
| `cluster_stat` | `"mass"` | test clusters by excess mass or by extent |
| `connectivity` | 6 | voxel neighbourhood: 6, 18 or 26 |
| `min_subjects` | 2 | voxels with fewer finite subjects are excluded |
| `threads` | package setting | OpenMP threads for this call |

Missing values are dropped subject by subject at each voxel. When coverage
differs between subjects, a voxel's t has its own degrees of freedom, which
is why the default spatial statistic is the z-equivalent of t. A voxel with
fewer than `min_subjects` finite subjects, or with zero variance, has no
statistic. It is excluded from the mask: it never exceeds a threshold, it does
not connect its neighbours into one cluster, and its spatial assays are `NA`.

## Whole-brain data

For real data the source is a set of subject contrast maps and a brain mask.
The call is the same:

```{r nifti, eval = FALSE}
files <- sprintf("derivatives/sub-%02d_task_beta.nii.gz", 1:35)
res <- gds(nifti_source(beta = files, subjects = sprintf("sub-%02d", 1:35)),
           format = "nifti", mask = "group_mask.nii.gz") |>
  reduce(method = "perm:onesample",
         options = list(n_perm = 5000, seed = 1, alternative = "two.sided",
                        spatial = c("tfce", "cluster"), cluster_p = 0.001)) |>
  compute()
write_nifti_assays(res, "group_maps",
                   assays = c("t_g", "p_fwer", "tfce", "p_tfce_fwer",
                              "cluster_id", "p_cluster_fwer"))
```

The permutations run in compiled code, in parallel across sign flips. Set
the thread count before loading the package with `FMRIGDS_THREADS` (or
`OMP_NUM_THREADS`), or per call with `options$threads`; the default is two
threads. On a 243,515-voxel mask with 35 subjects, 5,000 two-sided sign flips
computing max-T, TFCE and cluster mass together took about one minute with
eight threads on an Apple M-series laptop (about six minutes with one
thread); see `inst/examples/fmrigds_perm_spatial_benchmark.R`.
